title: Journey - Five Days of Gratitude - Day 5: Enough for today

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, a soft smile in the voice, unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Gratitude. <short pause> This is day five, Enough for Today. <short pause> It's the last day of this journey, and I'm so glad you're here. <short pause> We have one sentence left to learn... and then we'll put all five together.

Let yourself slow down. <short pause> Let both hands rest open, if that's comfortable. <short pause> Breathe in only as much air as you need. <short pause> Notice that you don't store it up. <short pause> You let it go... <short pause> and there is more.

All around us, there's a quiet voice that says, not yet. <short pause> Not enough saved. Not enough done. <short pause> Not young enough, or clever enough, or far enough along. <short pause> It moves the line each time we get near it. <short pause> And a heart that is always chasing the line finds it very hard to say thank you.

When Jesus taught His friends to pray, He gave them words for this. <short pause> He could have taught them to ask for a storehouse. <short pause> He taught them to ask for something that fits in one hand. <short pause> It is in Matthew chapter six, verse eleven.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: This day. <short pause> Not the whole year, all at once. <short pause> Daily bread. <short pause> Not a feast, and not crumbs. Bread. <short pause> And listen... He says us. <short pause> Give us. Our bread. <short pause> So this kind of enough is never just mine. <short pause> It has room at the table for someone else.

parts.style: warm reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: If you truly don't have enough today, this verse does not scold you. <short pause> It is a prayer for people who need bread. <short pause> You can ask Him plainly for what is missing, and you can let others help to bring it. <short pause> Being content doesn't mean you stop asking. <short pause> It means you can ask with an open hand.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: So ask, just for today. <short pause> What is the bread you need before this day ends? <short pause> Food, or money for it. Patience. An answer. A little courage. <short pause> Ask Him for that one portion, in your own words. <short pause> And then notice what is already on the table. <short pause> What has He given that is enough for this very minute?

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Think of the road these days have taken. <short pause> We came in through the gate, and began with who God is. <short pause> We followed a plain thing home to Him. <short pause> We opened one hand in the middle of what was hard. <short pause> We gave our thanks to a person, out loud. <short pause> Whether you walked every step of that or only some, you can pray where it has led.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Here is the fifth sentence. <short pause> It is enough. <short pause> Now all five, slowly. Let each one have its own breath. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> This is from You. <short pause> Even here. <short pause> Through them. <short pause> It is enough.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Once more, and this time they are yours. <short pause> I'll say each one softly, and you can pray it after me. <short pause> You are good... <short pause> This is from You... <short pause> Even here... <short pause> Through them... <short pause> It is enough.

Let's pray. <short pause> Our Father, give us this day our daily bread. <short pause> Thank You for who You are, for what You send, for staying in the hard places, and for the people You love me through. <short pause> When I forget, bring me back to the gate. <short pause> And make my enough big enough to share. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, warm, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: The journey ends here, but the prayer can come with you. <short pause> Choose one meal a day, and say your five sentences before the first bite. <short pause> It will take less time than the food takes to cool. <short pause> Thank you for walking these days with me. <short pause> Go in peace... and go with thanks.
